Theme

Latin word

colloquium

colloquium, colloquiī n.

noun, second declension

a conversation, a meeting for talks; an interview (for a job, with a journalist); a meeting for talks; talks, a meeting to negotiate

In this lexicon

  • dialogue

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BG 1.35, 1.43: ad colloquium vēnērunt (Lewis & Short); Cic. Phil. 12.26

  • interview

    the recommended word · modern · Traupman 334: colloquium, interview

  • meeting

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.43: eō ad colloquium vēnērunt (Lewis & Short)

  • negotiation

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BG 1.34.1: aliquem locum medium utrīsque conloquiō; Cic. Phil. 12.26: in Antōniī congressum colloquiumque veniendum est (Lewis & Short)

  • colloquium tēlephōnicum: talk on the phone

    modern

  • colloquium vīsificum: video call

    * our formation

Examples

  • in Antōniī congressum colloquiumque veniendum est

    we have to come to a meeting and talks with AntonyCic. Phil. 12.26 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for dialogue

  • hinc colloquium cum veniunt in ūnum locum loquendī causā

    hence colloquium, when people come together in one place in order to talkVarr. LL 6.57

    In the entry for interview

  • quī ab eō postulārent utī aliquem locum medium utrīsque conloquiō dēligeret: velle sēsē dē rē pūblicā et summīs utrīusque rēbus cum eō agere

    to ask him to choose some place halfway between them for talks: he wanted to negotiate with him about public affairs and matters of the highest importance to them bothCaes. BG 1.34.1

    In the entry for negotiation

  • Diēs conloquiō dictus est ex eō diē quīntus.

    The talks were fixed for the fifth day from then.Caes. BG 1.42

    In the entry for negotiation
